evidence_inputs.method: Judged from the two attached PNGs only (1400x900 RGB). Method: apart from the visual read, palette histograms and per-family run counting of the two named PNGs, plus a banded check that counts dark analytic crossings on sampled rows and tests for a blue companion within +-5 px over a +-7 row band (the +-7 rows cover a dash period, so a dash gap does not read as a missing level). No SVG was opened, rendered or read; the drawing script was consulted only for the line each finding is anchored to and never for a verdict.

Both window titles state the separation in millimetres (0.19, 0.88, 4.12), so the reader gets the number as well as the picture.

findings.summary: The diverted panel draws one blue curve solid where the in-figure legend says the cell family is dashed, so a reader who looks for a solid blue line has no explanation for it. The boundary-level contour of the read's field is drawn in the feature colour at 2.6 pt with the default solid style (the draw_flux_contours call at this line passes no linestyle), and it is plainly visible in the rendered panel: scanning rows 120-760 the outermost blue feature is present on 641 of 700 rows with a single jump above 6 px between consecutive rows, which is a continuous curve, against 104 such jumps in the limited panel where only the dashed family is drawn. The legend block reads 'cell field / dashed, small nulls' and neither caption mentions a solid cell contour, so the one solid blue line in the figure is unexplained ink that a reader can mistake for the analytic family drawn in the wrong colour.

findings.disposition: exempted: the boxes delimit the magnified windows, cost a reader nothing, and removing them would need a redraw of a figure that otherwise reads correctly; recorded so the next figure in this family does not repeat the frame
findings.summary: The two magnification windows carry complete four-sided boxes in #888888, which the repository's plotting rules exclude: every axis is despined and a 2D poloidal panel is drawn with its axis off, because a frame is furniture that adds no information. The frames are clearly visible in both attached panels as grey rectangles around each zoom. They do not distract from the data and they usefully delimit the magnified region, which is why this does not block, but they are the one piece of styled furniture on an otherwise axis-free figure and a redraw would remove them.

summary: I opened both attached PNGs and judged the pictures only: image-0.png is the diverted trial state (saddle null at the divertor, 'normal-form radius 107.13 mm' annotation, two magnified windows titled 'axis magnified, 0.19 mm apart' and 'X-point magnified, 0.88 mm apart') and image-1.png is the limited trial state (nested contours, no saddle, one window titled 'axis magnified, 4.12 mm apart'). The repair at 15f6cfddfd works: both contour families are now visible in both panels. On rows 350, 450 and 550 through the main panels every dark analytic crossing is accompanied by the dashed blue read contour within +-5 px over +-7 rows (0-2 unpaired of 22-29 crossings per row, the misses at the outermost level), and the whole-panel ink balance is 11,939 near-black against 11,117 feature-blue pixels in the diverted panel and 14,510 against 9,026 in the limited one, against 92 near-black in the same region before the repair. The null pairs, which previously merged into one mark, are separable in the windows: the large dark marker and the small feature-coloured one are about a marker-width apart and read as two. Six rubric items are reported per figure. No blocking defect survives. Two non-blocking findings are recorded: one solid blue curve (the boundary-level contour) contradicts the in-figure legend's 'cell field / dashed', and the two magnification windows carry full four-spine boxes that the repository's despine rule excludes. Nothing was edited, created, moved or redrawn; no SVG was opened and no image other than the two named PNGs was read.
